ls -l is a long form output. ls -1 is the item name only.

$ ls -l
total 0
-rw-r--r-- 1 sakuramboo users 0 Dec 13 10:35 foo1
-rw-r--r-- 1 sakuramboo users 0 Dec 13 10:35 foo2
-rw-r--r-- 1 sakuramboo users 0 Dec 13 10:35 foo3

$ ls -1
foo1
foo2
foo3

So, the benefit to using ls -1 is the lower memory requirements because there's less information to parse through. Which could also have a knock on effect of increased performance. Of course, on today's systems, the gains won't be noticed, but good to remember when you start writing bash scripts.
